The skipped assertion is a second, redundant activation channel: the case's primary activation evidence, SHOW HEAP OOS, executed and passed in this invocation, and inv-T14-0002 executes the skipped assertion on the debug build.

applicability.fixture: Identical, because it is the same run: the four rows of (id INT, v BIT VARYING) at 4,036 AA / 16,284 BB / 4,011 CC / 4,036 DD that the assertions judge are the rows SHOW HEAP OOS counted, in a database the case created, owns exclusively and deletes.
applicability.execution_path: IDENTICAL, which is why this is proven and not reused. The SHOW HEAP OOS statement ran in the same CTP invocation, against the same client-server server process, in the same session sequence as the INSERT it certifies -- once immediately after the committed INSERT and once after the restart. outstanding_coverage.note: Ticket 14 is the private tracer bullet: one case proving the private shell seam end to end, not coverage. The 49 assertable or observation-only requirements listed are everything this invocation did not execute, including the three ticket 13 executed on the public seam; the 12 BLOCKED and UNSUPPORTED requirements are deliberately absent from the list, because a case that cannot run is not a Delivery gap. Tickets 23 to 32 close the private-shell part of the list. ASSERTION COUNTS HERE ARE MEASURED, NOT DERIVED, which is the one place this seam is stronger than the public one: the shell runner writes one '<case>-<n> : OK|NOK' line per assertion into the case's .result file and reproduces them in feedback.log, so ticket 13's finding P4 (CTP SQL has no assertion counter) does not apply to the shell seam. Expected 16 rather than the oracle's 17 because assertion 17 is capability-gated on a debug build; the oracle states that split before the run. FOR TICKET 15: the launcher exits 0 on a failed case here exactly as it does on the SQL side -- the negative control att-T14-0025 reported Total Fail Case:1 with launcher exit status 0 -- so shell tooling must read result/shell/current_runtime_logs/test_status.data, never $?. FOR TICKET 17: the case took 14 seconds of its own time and the whole invocation 23 seconds on the release build, well inside the fast tier's 120-second per-case cap. The launcher's own testcase_timeout_in_secs was deliberately set to 900 rather than 120 so that CTP cannot SIGKILL a crash-recovery case mid-restart and destroy its evidence; that means the campaign's per-case cap is currently judged from the measured time rather than enforced by the harness, and enforcing it belongs to ticket 15. COEXISTENCE: att-T14-0016-bucket ran this case in one invocation together with the ten existing cases of the same issue bucket; it produced the same 16 OK and 1 SKIP as when run alone, and the install configuration and the testcase worktree came back unchanged. That run has no manifest of its own because it adds no coverage; its evidence is under evidence/ticket14/att-T14-0016-bucket/. THE CASE OUTCOME IN THIS MANIFEST IS THE CASE'S OWN, not CTP's success count: CTP has only PASS and FAIL per case, so the case writes PASS, FAIL or SKIP with a reason into <evidence>/case_outcome and the runner surfaces it. A run where SHOW HEAP OOS was unavailable would record SKIP there even with every executed assertion passing, because durability would be proved while the out-of-row path was never observed. This run's file reads PASS. The failure-preservation copy is itself checked in this revision: every step's exit status is tested and a failure is reported as a further NOK, because with CTP's snapshot channel switched off this copy is the only image a failing run leaves behind. att-T14-0025 exercised the path and journalled preservation|ok. The activation channel's own failure classifier has three outcomes, not two: only a syntax error is a capability gap, anything else is a failure of this case. Its controlled failure examples are in tools/checker_validation_classifier.sh. The activation channel reads its column positions from the output's own header, so a reordering in the engine's show_meta.c cannot be read silently as the wrong columns.
